speaker: narrator
en: In the City of Destruction, a man sat reading a Book. The more he read, the heavier his heart grew.
source: Part I, opening: 'I saw a man clothed with rags... a book in his hand, and a great burden upon his back.'

speaker: christian
en: This Book says our city will be burned with fire from heaven. What shall I do to be saved?
source: Part I: 'What shall I do?' / Acts 16:30

speaker: christian
en: And this burden on my back grows heavier every day.
source: Part I: the burden appears as he reads

speaker: family
en: You are tired, that is all. Sleep, and you will feel better in the morning.
source: Part I: his relations think 'some frenzy distemper had got into his head' and send him to bed

speaker: christian
en: Stay with them, or go?
source: Prototype choice

speaker: ui
en: Stay and hope the city improves
source: Prototype choice

speaker: ui
en: Leave and find the way
source: Prototype choice

speaker: narrator
en: He dreamed of red smoke over the rooftops. When he woke, the burden was heavier still.
source: Adaptation (no fire on people)

speaker: sign
en: Flee from the wrath to come.
source: Matthew 3:7 (KJV), quoted by Evangelist in Part I

speaker: townsfolk
en: There goes the man with the Book again.
source: Adaptation: neighbours mock him

speaker: townsfolk
en: He has gone soft in the head, poor fellow.
source: Adaptation: 'some mocked'

speaker: obstinate
en: Neighbour, where are you going? Come back with us!
source: Part I: Obstinate and Pliable 'resolved to fetch him back by force'

speaker: christian
en: I am going to an inheritance that cannot fade away. Come with me.
source: Part I: 'an inheritance incorruptible, undefiled, and that fadeth not away' (1 Peter 1:4)

speaker: obstinate
en: Tush! Away with your Book. Will you come back with us or no?
source: Part I: 'Tush, said Obstinate, away with your book'

speaker: christian
en: No, not I. I have laid my hand to the plough.
source: Part I, Luke 9:62

speaker: obstinate
en: Come, Pliable, let us go home. I will not keep company with such a fool.
source: Part I: 'I will be no companion of such misled, fantastical fellows'

speaker: pliable
en: Wait. If what he says is true, things are better where he is going. I will go with him.
source: Part I: 'My heart inclines to go with my neighbour'

speaker: obstinate
en: Then you are both fools. I am going home.
source: Part I: Obstinate goes back alone

speaker: pliable
en: Tell me more of the place we are going. Is it truly so good?
source: Part I: Pliable and Christian talk of the Celestial City

speaker: christian
en: There is a kingdom there that will never end, and crowns of glory for those who reach it.
source: Part I: 'an endless kingdom to be inhabited, and everlasting life'

speaker: evangelist
en: Why are you crying?
source: Part I: 'Wherefore dost thou cry?'

speaker: christian
en: Sir, I read that I am condemned to die and after that to come to judgement. I am not ready.
source: Part I

speaker: evangelist
en: Then why do you stand still?
source: Part I: 'Why standest thou still?'

speaker: christian
en: Because I do not know which way to go.
source: Part I: 'Because I know not whither to go'

speaker: evangelist
en: Do you see yonder wicket gate?
source: Part I: 'Do you see yonder wicket-gate?'

speaker: christian
en: No.
source: Part I

speaker: evangelist
en: Do you see yonder shining light?
source: Part I: 'Do you see yonder shining light?'

speaker: christian
en: I think I do.
source: Part I: 'I think I do'

speaker: evangelist
en: Keep that light in your eye, and go straight toward it. There you will find the gate. Knock, and you will be told what to do.
source: Part I: 'Keep that light in your eye, and go up directly thereto'

speaker: sign
en: Read the Book when you are unsure of the way. It will show you what you cannot see.
source: Mechanic hint (The Book reveals hidden platforms)

speaker: narrator
en: So he began to run, crying, 'Life, life, eternal life!'
source: Part I: 'Life! life! eternal life!'
